Title: Ministry Of The People Distributes Over $69,000 In SEED Grants To San Fernando Entrepreneurs
Article:
The Ministry of the People, Social Development and Family Services (MPSDFS) continued the distribution of its Sowing Empowerment through Entrepreneurial Development (SEED) Grants today, Wednesday September 3, 2025 at the Gulf View Community Centre, San Fernando.
The Honourable Vandana Mohit, Minister of the People, Social Development and Family Services, led the distribution during which five (5) deserving clients received SEED Grants valued at sixtynine thousand, six hundred and seventeen dollars ($69,617.00), to the benefit of a total of twentythree (23) persons from the community.
Minister Mohit congratulated the recipients and shared her hope of seeing their businesses thrive by being able to walk into one of their businesses in the near future as a testament to their growth and success. She reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to bringing services directly to the people, ensuring that citizens can access Government’s support in their own communities.
One of the recipients, Mr. Joel Osborne, expressed his appreciation for the timely support, stating that he was grateful for the quick response to his application. He added that the grant left him feeling encouraged and empowered by the opportunity to move forward in furthering his business.
The SEED Grant, valued at up to $15,000.00 per recipient, is administered through the National Social Development Programme (NSDP). It provides disadvantaged citizens with the resources to initiate or expand their micro-enterprises by supplying equipment, materials, or specialised training.
The Ministry will continue its community-based SEED distributions across the country as part of its mission to empower citizens, reduce poverty, and strengthen families.
Author: TTT News

Title: 10 Held In Foiled Plot To Harm Law Enforcement Officer
Article:
A covert tactical operation, activated by Commissioner of Police Allister Gueverro and Deputy Commissioner of Police Suzette Martin, successfully disrupted and neutralized a coordinated plot to harm a member of law enforcement stationed at the Eastern Correctional and Rehabilitation Centre (ECRC).
10 persons were detained and 1 firearm was recovered.
According to the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service, upon entering the vicinity of the Centre, officers engaged multiple suspects who attempted to elude capture.
The threat, which contributed to the declaration of a State of Emergency, continues to be monitored and this latest action underscores the evolving tactics of criminal networks, operating both within and beyond prison walls.
The TTPS noted that while the immediate plot was disrupted, the TTPS continues to monitor known gang affiliates outside of custody who may still be intent on executing the directives of their incarcerated leaders.
Commissioner Guevarro commended the officers and emphasized the TTPS’ commitment to the protection of all.
Author: Ayanna Carter

Title: TTUTA: Police In Schools Must Be Temporary
Article:
President of the Trinidad and Tobago Unified Teachers’ Association (TTUTA), Martin Lum Kin, says support will be given to any initiative that “brings a level of normalcy to schools that are threatened by violence and indiscipline.”
Responding to the announcement by Minister of Education, Dr. Michael Dowlath, that police officers will be posted to 50 priority secondary schools in Trinidad and Tobago, and that dedicated patrols will occur at 10 primary and 10 secondary schools for consistent coverage and rapid response, Mr. Lum Kin says armed officers will not be supported.
“The perception as well as the risk associated with armed persons on our nation’s schools is not needed at this time. TTUTA submits that the placement of law enforcement officers should be a short-term and temporary measure as the Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago and other organisations look at addressing crime and criminality which affects our communities and our schools.”
Minister of Homeland Security, Roger Alexander, in response to media questions on the issue on Thursday, assured that police officers stationed at schools will use non-lethal methods to defuse situations. He said the move is in full accordance with the law.
Author: Ayanna Carter

Title: Major Law Enforcement Operation “Summer Slam” Nets 32 Arrests, Firearms, Narcotics, And Ammunition
Article:
In a concerted effort to disrupt criminal activity and enhance public safety, a coordinated police operation dubbed “Summer Slam” was conducted across several communities, resulting in the arrest of 32 individuals, execution of 14 warrants, and multiple seizures of firearms, ammunition, and narcotics.
The operation, which included 42 stop and search exercises, led to the following major outcomes:
ARRESTS MADE:
Firearm, Ammunition & Robbery Offences:
One suspect held for Driving without Driver’s Permit and Certificate of Insurance; Possession of 3 rounds of 9mm ammunition; Robbery with Violence.
One suspect held for Possession of 198 grams of cannabis; Robbery with Violence.
Two suspects held for Robbery enquiries.
Two suspects held for Larceny enquiries.
Drug-Related Offences:
Suspect held for possession of 11 cannabis plants.
One Suspect held – Warrant for Possession of Cocaine.
One Suspect held – Warrant for Possession of Cocaine.
Violent Crimes:
One Suspect held – Enquiries re: Malicious Wounding.
Burglary Investigations:
Two suspects held – Enquiries re: Burglary in St. Margaret’s and other areas.
Breach of Protection Orders:
One suspect held – Two counts of Breach of Protection Order.
AFFILIATION AND OTHER WARRANTS EXECUTED:
Twelve persons were arrested on Affiliation Warrants totaling over $66,000. And eight persons held for enquiries.
ITEMS SEIZED:
Firearms & Ammunition
• Two (2) Homemade Shotguns
• Two (2) 12-gauge cartridges
• Three (3) 9mm rounds
Narcotics
• 198 grams of cannabis
• 11 cannabis plants
TRAFFIC & SAFETY ENFORCEMENT:
• 14 Fixed Penalty Notices issued for various traffic violations.
The Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) remains committed to proactive enforcement strategies that target violent crime, drug trafficking, and public safety breaches. The “Summer Slam” operation underscores our unwavering dedication to maintaining law and order, and we urge members of the public to continue supporting our efforts by sharing information anonymously via our hotlines.
Investigations are ongoing.
Author: TTT News

Title: Anti-Crime Exercise Yields Seizure Of High-Powered Weapon In Diego Martin
Article:
A coordinated anti-crime exercise was conducted within the West End Police District, between the hours of 10:30am and 1:30pm on Thursday 4th September, 2025.
The operation formed part of ongoing efforts by the Trinidad and Tobago Police Service (TTPS) to reduce the prevalence of illegal firearms and enhance public safety.
The exercise was sanctioned by Senior Superintendent Williams, Superintendent Gyan, and W/ASP Aguilleria, coordinated by Ag/Insp Perry and Sgt. Joefield, and supervised by W/Ag Sgt. Bovell.
Operational support was provided by Cpl Carter, PCs Belfon, and Mercer, of the West End Police Station.
As a result of surveillance conducted on a commercial property located along North Coast Road, Diego Martin, officers executed a search of a security booth situated on the compound. During the search, an AR-15 rifle, fitted with a magazine and strap, was discovered concealed in the ceiling of the booth.
The item was safely retrieved, processed, and seized. It was taken to the West End Police Station where it remains secured pending further investigation led by PC Belfon.
The TTPS continues to urge members of the public to share any information they may have regarding illegal activities by contacting 555, 999, or the nearest police station. All information will be treated with the strictest confidence.
Investigations are ongoing.
Author: TTT News

Title: Seven Arrested During SOE Operation In Point Fortin
Article:
A joint State of Emergency (SOE) operation was carried out in the Point Fortin district between the hours of 3pm and 8pm on Thursday September 4th, 2025, resulting in the arrest of seven suspects.
The exercise was spearheaded by Senior Superintendent Thompson and Superintendent Simon, and was coordinated by Assistant Superintendents Corrie, Forbes, and Lewis, as well as Inspector Prescott. Supervision was provided by Inspector Sirju, Sgts. Smith, and Breedy.
The team comprised officers from the Point Fortin Criminal Investigations Department (CID), Point Fortin Police Station, and the South-Western Division Task Force.
During the operation, officers conducted house searches under the authority of Sections 8 and 13 of Legal Notice 240 of the Emergency Powers Regulations, 2025 and several houses in the Cap- De- Ville area were searched.
Additionally, several known drug blocks in the area were searched. As a result, seven individuals were arrested, four in Techier Village and three in Chin Kit Park, Point Fortin for assembling for the purpose of gambling, an offence under the current SOE regulations.
Inquiries are ongoing.
Author: TTT News

Title: Ministers Back US Military Efforts To Curb Regional Drug And Arms Trade
Article:
The Government remains confident that the deployment of US military forces in the Caribbean is aimed at stemming the illicit drug and arms trade.
US officials allege the vessel destroyed in the waters off the southern Caribbean on Tuesday was operated by Venezuela’s Tren de Aragua gang and was carrying narcotics bound for Trinidad and Tobago. The strike claimed the lives of eleven people on board the vessel.
Minister of Defence, Wayne Sturge, responded to questions about the incident at Thursday’s Post-Cabinet Media Conference.
“There’s no basis for a deployment of our forces at this stage. Nothing has happened to warrant that. What took place in terms of the air strike took place in international waters and in pursuance of one sovereign state pursuing their own interests against persons who are acting in a manner that is inimical to their interest. That has nothing to do with Trinidad and Tobago.”
And Minister of Homeland Security Roger Alexander reiterated that the Government welcomes the assistance of the United States in fighting the illicit drug trade. He pointed to the well-known fact that Trinidad and Tobago is a trans-shipment point for the entry of narcotics and illegal firearms.
“Are you witnessing what is happening on the nation’s streets in terms of what type of firearms are being used? We do not manufacture firearms here, so they are coming in from somewhere. So if the United States says it is coming from this angle, together with the intelligence we have, then we should welcome that. Every citizen of this country should welcome that.”
Author: Karen Cozier-Phillip

Title: Man Charged With Murder In Connection To Death Of Ravi Pandhorie
Article:
A 43-year-old man is scheduled to appear before a High Court Master, charged with murder following the death of Ravi Pandhorie.
The accused, who has no fixed address, is expected to appear before the North Court ‘C’ on Friday September 5th, 2025.
The charge arises from an incident which occurred on August 10th, 2025, at Gilber Street, Felicity, Chaguanas in which the victim, Ravi Pandhorie, was wounded and subsequently warded at the Mt. Hope Hospital. He later succumbed to his injuries on August 14th, 2025.
Following investigations led by WPC Nestor of the Homicide Bureau of Investigations, Region 3, the suspect was arrested during an operation in the Felicity, Chaguanas area on 2nd September, 2025.
Subsequently, an audience was held with Acting Director of Public Prosecutions, Sabrina Dougdeen-Jagal, on September 4th, 2025. Instructions were then given for the suspect to be charged with murder on the same day.
Author: TTT News

Title: Five Held, Two Firearms, Ammunition And Narcotics Seized In SOE Operations
Article:
Five suspects were arrested and two firearms and quantities of ammunition and narcotics seized during ongoing State of Emergency Operations conducted across the country this week.
In the Tobago Division, officers of the Gang and Intelligence Unit conducted an exercise between 3:15pm and 6pm on Tuesday September 2nd, 2025, during which they proceeded to a hotel at Arnos Vale.
A search of the compound was conducted which resulted in the discovery of one AR-15 rifle loaded with a magazine containing two rounds of ammunition.
Meanwhile, one 53-year-old of Moriah was arrested in connection with a report of rape by the officers in the same exercise.
In the Bamboo Settlement #2 district, officers conducted an exercise yesterday afternoon which resulted in the interception of a motor vehicle with three occupants, including a Spanish-speaking national.
A search resulted in the officers finding one revolver loaded with two rounds of ammunition in the possession of the Spanish-speaking national.
The 38-year-old suspect was arrested in connection with the find.
In the Eastern Division, Task Force officers, with the assistance of the Canine Unit, carried out a State of Emergency Operation in the Sangre Grande district between 2am and 5am, today, Thursday September 4th, 2025.
During the exercise two suspects were arrested: a 37-year-old man and a 19-year-old woman for possession of quantities of cannabis and ammunition.
And in the Central Division, officers arrested a 27-year-old woman for possession of a quantity of cannabis and TT$24,900 in cash.
The exercise, coordinated by Supt. Glodon and ASP Hernandez, was conducted by officers of the Cunupia CID, Guard and Emergency Branch, Canine Unit and the Cunupia Police Station.
Investigations are ongoing into all of the above matters.
Author: TTT News

Title: Police Commissioner Supports US Strike, Issues Warning To ‘Fishers Of Fortune’
Article:
Commissioner of Police, Allister Guevarro, is warning individuals involved in the illicit drug trade via the waters of the Caribbean to cease and desist — or face the full force of the US military.
His comments come in the wake of a recent US military strike on a vessel suspected of transporting narcotics in the southern Caribbean.
“I am grateful for the decisive US intervention. The resources deployed will undoubtedly place a significant dent in narcotics trafficking across the southern Caribbean. Let this serve as a clear warning to our fishers of fortune who board their pirogues chasing perilous tides of profit. The waters have changed. If you are heading out to sea, it’s time to start catching fish to assist in feeding our nation and not as drug smugglers masquerading as fishermen because when the US armada comes calling, I wish you luck in treating with what will not be a happy ending. I have absolutely no pity on anyone caught in that net, be it carite or criminal.”
Author: TTT News
